# `gen.sweep`: Sweep

Carries a cross section along a path into rails, trims, frames, handles and cables, with twist and taper.

- Category: gen
- Version: 1
- Complexity: O(path points x profile points) plus O(p log p) per cap
- Flags: undoable, creates_groups, creates_objects
- Also known as: sweep, curve bevel, extrude along path, loft along path, follow me, tube along curve

The cross section is seen looking along the path (x right, y up) and rides on rotation-minimizing frames, so it never spins on its own; `twist` turns it on purpose and `scale` tapers it from start to end. Sharp path corners are mitered so the section keeps its thickness (a frame swept along a closed rectangle). `up` sets which way the section's y points at the start (+Y by default).

**Cross sections:** `{"rectangle": [w, h]}`, `{"circle": r}` (quad-grid caps; see also `gen.pipe`), points `[x, y]` (`profile_closed: false` for open trims), or `{"curve": name}`. **Paths:** points (`smooth_path` for a curve through them, `path_closed` for loops) or `{"curve": name}`; built from a path curve, the result lands where the curve is.

**Groups:** `side`, `cap_start`, `cap_end`, and `profile_<i>` per side of a rectangle or point section. Section corners and path joints sharper than 30 degrees get sharp edges.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `caps` | `boolean` | `true` | Fills the ends of a closed cross section on an open path. |
| `name` | `string \| null` | - | Object name; a free name such as `sweep_1` is picked when omitted. |
| `parent` | `string \| null` | - | Parent object (name, path or id); top level when omitted. |
| `path` | `Path` | required | The path the cross section follows. |
| `path_closed` | `boolean` | `false` | Joins the last inline path point back to the first. |
| `position` | `[Length, Length, Length] \| null` | - | Origin position in the parent's space. Built from a path curve, the result takes the curve's place (parent and transform) unless `parent` or `position` is given. |
| `profile` | `Section` | required | The cross section. |
| `profile_closed` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether inline profile points close into a loop (open profiles make trims and ribbons). |
| `resolution` | `number` | `6` | Segments per curved span of Bezier curves. |
| `scale` | `[number, number]` | `[1.0,1.0]` | Cross section scale at the start and the end (taper). |
| `segments` | `number \| null` | - | Points around a circle cross section; adapts to its size when omitted. |
| `smooth_path` | `boolean` | `false` | A smooth Bezier through inline path points instead of straight segments. |
| `twist` | `Angle` | `0.0` | Turn of the cross section from start to end (degrees); closed paths need whole turns. |
| `up` | `[number, number, number] \| null` | - | Direction the cross section's y leans toward at the start. |

## Examples

```json
{"name":"rail","path":{"curve":"path"},"profile":{"rectangle":["4cm","2cm"]}}
```

Result: `created rail (o:4) sweep 1.02 m x 20 mm x 1.02 m: 10 faces (20 tris; budget 6,000)`

```json
{"name":"horn","path":[[0,0,0],[0,0.3,0],[0.2,0.5,0]],"profile":{"circle":"4cm"},"scale":[1,0.1],"segments":12,"smooth_path":true}
```

Result: `created horn (o:4) sweep 0.2464 m x 0.5049 m x 77.27 mm: 210 faces (420 tris; budget 6,000)`
